name: VIX (CBOE Volatility Index)
what: 30-day implied volatility priced into S&P 500 options; the market's pricing of near-term risk
why: VIX is the classic leading/coincident crash indicator. It closed at 82.69 on 2020-03-16 (one of the highest closes on record), spiked from 17.31 to 37.32 (+116%) in a single day during the 2018-02-05 "Volmageddon" event (triggering forced liquidation of short-VIX products that dragged down equity indices), and repeatedly touched 70-80 in October-November 2008. Sharp VIX spikes tend to coincide with, or lead by 1-2 days, single-day equity crashes
warning_threshold: VIX > 25 (above the historical 80th percentile; market entering a stress zone)
danger_threshold: VIX > 35 or a single-day gain > 40% (historical crisis-onset threshold; triggered cascading sell-offs in 2018, 2020 and 2008)

api.method: GET (requires a browser UA header, otherwise the request may be rejected)

name: VIX Term Structure Inversion (VIX/VIX3M)
what: Ratio of near-term VIX to 3-month VIX (VIX3M), measuring whether the term structure has flipped from normal contango into backwardation
why: In a normal market VIX < VIX3M (ratio < 1, contango); when a spike in near-term fear pushes the ratio above 1 (inversion/backwardation), this has repeatedly and precisely flagged crisis onsets historically: the ratio broke above 1.0-1.2 during the 2015-08 China devaluation flash crash, the 2018-02 Volmageddon, and the week the COVID crash began (2020-02-24 through 03), with the S&P 500 subsequently falling more than 10% within 1-3 weeks

api.method: GET (requires a browser UA header); fetch both endpoints separately and divide
api.parse: VIX: chart.result[0].meta.regularMarketPrice; VIX3M likewise; ratio = VIX / VIX3M

name: CBOE SKEW Index (Tail-Risk Index)
what: Tail-risk pricing implied by deep out-of-the-money S&P 500 options — a gauge of "black swan" premium and left-tail thickness
why: SKEW > 140 is generally considered a sign that the market is paying a premium for extreme downside tail events; SKEW repeatedly printed highs of 145-150+ from late 2017 into early 2018 right before the 2018-02 Volmageddon, and it also held elevated ahead of the early-2020 crash. Note this indicator is noisy and usually needs confirmation from a simultaneous rise in VIX
danger_threshold: SKEW > 150 with VIX rising in tandem (double confirmation)

api.sample_value: 148.51 (live-tested on 2026-07-16, already in the warning zone)

name: MOVE Index (ICE BofA MOVE, Bond Volatility)
what: Implied volatility on U.S. Treasury options; the bond market's equivalent of VIX
why: Bond-market volatility often leads equities — MOVE spiked to a record 198.66 during the March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank crisis, which was followed by a chain of regional-bank stock collapses; it also spiked to 163 during the March 2020 COVID shock. Normal readings usually sit between 60 and 90
danger_threshold: MOVE > 160 (historical trigger level for banking/credit crises)

name: High-Yield OAS (ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread)
what: Option-adjusted spread of U.S. high-yield (junk) bonds over Treasuries; the pricing of credit-market risk
why: Widening credit spreads tend to lead equity declines by 1-4 weeks ("credit leads equity"). The spread spiked to a FRED-record 21.82% in December 2008, and jumped from 3.5% to 10.87% in under a month during the March 2020 COVID shock, which was followed by a secondary equity leg-down
warning_threshold: HY OAS > 5.0% (widened more than 100bp off recent lows)

api.method: GET, free CSV, no key required
api.parse: Second column of the last row of the CSV (%)

name: 10-Year / 2-Year Treasury Spread (10Y-2Y)
what: Spread between long- and short-end U.S. Treasury yields; the shape of the yield curve
why: New York Fed research shows every U.S. recession since 1955 has been preceded by a 10Y-2Y inversion (negative spread), with an average lead time of 6-24 months; the August 2019 inversion was followed by the 2020 recession (accelerated by COVID), and the July 2022 inversion was followed by a marked slowdown in 2023-24. "Re-steepening" after inversion (flipping from negative back to positive) tends to be a more precise signal that a recession/equity downturn is imminent
danger_threshold: Rapid re-steepening back to positive after inversion (historical harbinger of recession onset)

api.method: GET, free CSV, no key required
api.parse: Second column of the last row of the CSV (percentage points)

name: CBOE Put/Call Ratio
what: Market-wide put option volume divided by call option volume; a gauge of options-market sentiment
why: Extremely low ratios (<0.5-0.6) often accompany excessive market optimism and chasing behavior, acting as a contrarian near-term top signal — e.g. equity put/call stayed below 0.5 for several days ahead of the January 2018 top; extremely high ratios (>1.0-1.2) tend to appear in the late stage of panic selling, marking short-term bottoms
danger_threshold: Equity Put/Call > 1.2 in a single day (acute panic) or below 0.5 for several consecutive days (dangerous complacency)

api.method: GET, page scraping (CBOE's raw CSV endpoint at cdn.cboe.com returns 403 AccessDenied to programmatic requests; the HTML table on the page must be parsed instead — not a clean JSON feed)
api.parse: The "TOTAL PUT/CALL RATIO" and "EQUITY PUT/CALL RATIO" values in the page table
api.sample_value: Total 0.93 / Equity 0.69 (live-tested on 2026-07-16 via page scraping, not a structured API)

name: Market Breadth (NYSE New Highs - New Lows / Advance-Decline Divergence)
what: Number of stocks making new 52-week highs minus those making new lows, and whether the advance-decline line is diverging from the index
why: Ahead of the October 2007 S&P top, breadth indicators (new-high counts, the advance-decline line) had already been weakening for weeks, forming the classic "price makes a new high, breadth doesn't" top divergence; signals like the Hindenburg Omen are built on simultaneous surges in new highs and new lows. Deteriorating breadth tends to lead index tops by 2-8 weeks
warning_threshold: New lows exceed new highs for 5+ consecutive trading days while the index still makes new highs (divergence)
danger_threshold: Advance-decline line falls more than 10% off its high while the index remains close to its high (deep top divergence)

api.parse: Could not be live-tested — the relevant CBOE/CNBC/Nasdaq/Stooq endpoints all require authentication or return 403/CAPTCHA blocks; can only be checked manually on the web page
api.sample_value: Not obtained (honest disclosure: no free API; manual web-page inspection only)

name: FINRA Margin Debt
what: Outstanding margin-account debit balances held by U.S. brokerage customers (monthly data); a gauge of market leverage
why: Margin debt hitting repeated record highs has often coincided with market tops (the March 2000 dot-com top, the July 2007 pre-subprime-crisis peak, and the October 2021 record of $935B after which U.S. equities turned bearish); a sharp drop in margin debt from a high (deleveraging) tends to accompany crashes and become a self-reinforcing accelerant of the decline
warning_threshold: Month-over-month decline of more than 5% (deleveraging signal)
danger_threshold: Month-over-month decline of more than 10%, or a drawdown of more than 15% from a historical high (historical crisis pattern)

api.method: GET, free direct xlsx download, no key required (the filename contains a date string but the file content is continuously updated, not a fixed snapshot)
api.parse: Parse the first worksheet of the xlsx; the first data row is the latest month: column 2 = Debit Balances (margin debt, in millions of USD)
api.sample_value: May 2026: 1,415,557 million USD (data carries roughly a 6-week publication lag; a monthly, not real-time, indicator)

name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
what: A composite 0-100 sentiment score combining 7 market indicators (momentum, strength, breadth, put/call, junk-bond demand, volatility, safe-haven demand)
why: Readings collapsing into the single digits / extreme-fear zone (<20) have repeatedly coincided with market bottoms (multiple 2022 bear-market rally launch points, the December 2018 low); readings above 90 in the extreme-greed zone often precede short-term topping pullbacks (as before the January 2018 top and the November 2021 top, both of which were in extreme greed)
danger_threshold: < 10 accompanied by an actual sustained decline (genuine panic rather than a sentiment overshoot), or > 90 (historical topping zone)

api.method: GET, requires Referer: https://www.cnn.com/markets/fear-and-greed and a browser UA, otherwise returns 418

name: BTC Perpetual Funding Rate
what: The funding rate settled every 8 hours between perpetual-futures longs and shorts; a positive rate means longs pay shorts (long crowding)
why: A persistently extreme positive funding rate (annualized 50%+) tends to mark over-crowded leveraged longs — ahead of the 2021-05-19 crash, BTC funding rates on major exchanges held at 0.1-0.3%/8h (annualized over 100%) for multiple days, followed by roughly $8.6 billion in single-day liquidations; funding turning deeply negative is more commonly seen after panic sell-offs, when shorts become crowded
warning_threshold: Annualized funding rate > 50% (single-period rate roughly 0.05-0.06%/8h or above)
danger_threshold: Annualized funding rate > 100% (single-period rate roughly 0.1%/8h or above), or deeply negative below -30% annualized

api.method: GET, public endpoint, no key required
api.sample_value: 0.0000374281947186 (single period), annualized ≈4.10% (live-tested on 2026-07-16, normal, on the low side)

name: Open Interest (OI) and OI/Market-Cap Ratio
what: The notional value of open derivatives positions, and its ratio to the total market cap of the underlying asset; a gauge of leverage buildup
why: OI climbing rapidly while price is flat or rising, with weak spot volume, is the textbook precursor of "leverage stacking up, fragility rising" — the OI/mcap ratio was at a cyclical high ahead of both the May 2021 and June 2022 mass-liquidation events; a sudden drop in OI typically means forced deleveraging (liquidation) has already occurred
warning_threshold: OI rises more than 20% within 3 days while spot price rises less than 5% (leverage diverging from price)
danger_threshold: OI rises more than 15% in a single day (rapid buildup, sharply elevated liquidation risk)

api.method: GET, both endpoints free, no key required
api.parse: OKX: data[0].oiUsd; CoinGecko: bitcoin.usd_market_cap; ratio = oiUsd / usd_market_cap (note: this is OKX's single-exchange BTC contract OI, not network-wide aggregated OI — full aggregation requires paid Coinglass API; this is a feasible free proxy indicator)
api.sample_value: OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP OI ≈$1.97B, BTC-USD-SWAP OI ≈$467M; combined ≈$2.44B; BTC total market cap ≈$1.285T; OKX share ≈0.19% (live-tested on 2026-07-16, OKX-only basis)

name: Network-wide Liquidation Volume
what: Notional value of derivatives positions forcibly closed due to insufficient margin over the trailing 24 hours
why: Large-scale liquidations are the direct manifestation of a leverage cascade unwinding — network-wide liquidations reached roughly $8.6 billion in a single day on 2021-05-19 (a record at the time), and on 2020-03-12 ("Black Thursday") BitMEX alone saw over $1 billion liquidated, triggering a single-day halving of Bitcoin's price; consecutive days of liquidations in the low-billions often mark short-term extreme bottoms/tops

api.method: GET, public endpoint, no key required (returns only OKX's own tick-by-tick BTC-USDT perpetual liquidation records, not network-wide aggregated amounts; full aggregation requires the paid Coinglass API — this endpoint can only serve as a real-time proxy signal; for aggregated figures, check the check_url manually)
api.parse: response.data[0].details array, each entry containing bkPx (liquidation price), sz (size), posSide, ts; sum manually over a chosen time window
api.sample_value: Live-tested and obtained OKX's recent tick-by-tick liquidation records (e.g. bkPx=64116.1, sz=10 contracts, etc.); no network-wide total was aggregated

name: Annualized Futures Basis
what: The premium of quarterly futures contracts over the spot index, converted to an annualized yield
why: The basis is a long-standing quantitative gauge of leveraged-long sentiment and cash-and-carry funding costs — ahead of the April-May 2021 bull-market top, the basis reached over 30% annualized (cash-and-carry arbitrage extremely crowded), before turning negative in the subsequent crash; the basis turning negative or near zero commonly appears during panic sell-offs/capital flight
warning_threshold: Annualized basis > 15% (overheated sentiment) or < 0% (flips to backwardation, a panic signal)
danger_threshold: Annualized basis > 30% (historical top zone) or deeply negative basis (< -10%, acute panic)

api.method: GET, both free, no key required; basis = (quarterly contract price - spot index price) / spot index price, then annualized by remaining days to expiry
api.parse: Quarterly contract: data[0].last; spot index: data[0].idxPx; time to expiry can be computed from expTime returned by /api/v5/public/instruments?instType=FUTURES&instFamily=BTC-USD
api.sample_value: 2026-09-25 contract at 64574.2 vs. spot index 64114.2, basis 0.72%, ~70.8 days remaining, annualized ≈3.70% (live-tested on 2026-07-16, neutral-to-mild zone)

name: Stablecoin Total Market Cap Change
what: Combined market cap of major stablecoins such as USDT/USDC — representing on-hand "dry powder" ready to deploy and systemic risk exposure
why: Single- or multi-day drops in stablecoin market cap tend to correspond to systemic depeg risk events: the Terra/UST collapse in May 2022 wiped out roughly $18 billion of UST market cap within days (and triggered a broader market-wide panic sell-off); during the March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank crisis, USDC briefly depegged to $0.87, with related market cap shrinking by roughly $3 billion in a single day. Sustained multi-day net outflows also reflect capital leaving the crypto ecosystem
warning_threshold: Total market cap falls more than 1% in a single day
danger_threshold: Total market cap falls more than 3% in a single day, or a major stablecoin's price deviates more than 1% from $1 (depeg warning)

api.parse: Find the element with id=='stablecoins' in the returned array and take its market_cap field

name: Exchange BTC Net Inflow
what: Net amount of Bitcoin flowing from off-exchange wallets into centralized exchanges; a gauge of potential sell pressure/accumulation intent
why: Large net inflows to exchanges typically precede selling (holders moving coins to exchanges to prepare to sell) — abnormal spikes in exchange BTC balances/net inflow (per CryptoQuant/Glassnode data) were observed around the November 2022 FTX collapse and ahead of most major sell-offs historically; sustained net outflows tend to correspond to accumulation and bullish sentiment
danger_threshold: Single-day net inflow > 25,000 BTC, or net inflow amplifying for 3 consecutive days (historical pre-sell-off pattern)

api.parse: Could not be live-tested — the core data sources for this indicator, CryptoQuant and Glassnode, are both paid APIs (the free tiers don't include exchange-flow detail); the public pages also require login/subscription to view full figures, with only summary charts publicly visible
api.sample_value: Not obtained (honest disclosure: no free real-time API; requires a CryptoQuant/Glassnode paid subscription, or manual inspection of public chart trends)

name: Coinbase Premium Index
what: The premium of Coinbase's BTC price (representing U.S. institutional/regulated capital) over offshore exchanges such as Binance/OKX
why: A sustained deeply negative premium typically reflects U.S.-led capital selling/risk-off flight — the Coinbase premium rarely turned deeply negative for multiple consecutive days as it did during the November 2022 FTX collapse; a rising premium often precedes rallies during U.S. trading hours ("U.S. capital buying leads the tape")
warning_threshold: Premium < -0.1% sustained for more than 6 hours
danger_threshold: Premium < -0.3% (historical crisis-period level, as seen during the FTX collapse)

api.method: GET, both free, no key required; premium = (Coinbase price - OKX price) / OKX price × 100%
api.sample_value: Coinbase 64,085.1 vs. OKX 64,140.0, premium ≈-0.086% (live-tested on 2026-07-16, normal minor fluctuation range)

name: Crypto Fear & Greed Index
what: A composite 0-100 crypto-market sentiment score combining volatility, trading volume, social media, Bitcoin dominance, and Google search trends
why: Readings collapsing to single digits ("extreme fear") have repeatedly coincided with cyclical bottoms — the index fell to around 10 during the November 2022 FTX collapse; readings above 90 ("extreme greed") commonly appear near bull-market tops, e.g. the index held in the 85-95 range around Bitcoin's all-time high in November 2021
danger_threshold: < 10 (historic-level panic, as during the FTX collapse) or > 90 (historic-level topping zone, as around the November 2021 top)

api.sample_value: 25, Extreme Fear (live-tested on 2026-07-16, in the extreme-fear warning zone)

name: Estimated Leverage Ratio (ELR)
what: The ratio of notional open derivatives interest to exchange BTC/ETH reserves; a gauge of systemic leverage relative to exchange holdings
why: Glassnode's ELR rising steadily while price stalls has historically preceded multiple liquidation-driven deleveraging events (e.g. May 2021, June 2022), making it a core tool for judging whether "the market has been inflated by leverage"; this indicator itself is a paid Glassnode Studio Pro metric with no public free API
danger_threshold: ELR at a historical high (>0.25, the general pre-crisis level per Glassnode's historical data) with funding rates simultaneously turning positive and rising (double confirmation)

api.parse: Could not be live-tested — this indicator is a Glassnode Studio paid-only metric (Advanced/Professional subscription); the equivalent CryptoQuant indicator likewise requires payment; the free tier does not provide this data
api.sample_value: Not obtained (honest disclosure: no free API; requires a Glassnode/CryptoQuant paid subscription or manual inspection of paid charts)
